title: Ezra the Scribe Comes to Jerusalem
reflectionText: Three times the account says the same thing: the good hand of his God was on Ezra. A foreign king funded the journey, opened his treasury, and sent Ezra home with authority — and Ezra saw whose hand was behind it. He had set his heart to study the law, to do it, and to teach it; and when it was done, he blessed the God who had put it all in the king's heart. Where do you see a hand behind the doors that have opened for you?
editorialNotes: PAL Daily supervised production 2026-07-26, Batch G. Ezra 7:1-28. The long genealogy (7:1-5) is compressed to 'a descendant of Aaron the chief priest' and the king's decree (7:12-26) is summarized faithfully without altering its terms. Keeps the threefold refrain 'the good hand of his God on him' (7:6,9,28), Ezra's heart set to seek/do/teach the law (7:10), and his closing blessing of God (7:27-28). WEB 'Yahweh'; KJV 'the Lord'.
